content:
harper: quick note - ran into a nasty parity bug in the sampleapp rerank/embed helper when retries occur. Triggered only on model_dim=640 and batch sizes >= 7.

harper: minimal repro (Node):
```js
// send.js (node-sdk v0.11.0)
const ids = docs.map((d,i)=>d.id||`r${i}`);
const vectors = docs.map(d=>padTo(d.embed, 640));
await client.rerank.batch({ model: 'sim-640', body: { ids, vectors } });
```

harper: behavior: if a shard times out and runtime does fallback, runtime returns an explicit `ids` array in a different order. Node helper maps scores by index and we attach wrong scores to docs -> top-k incorrect.

leo: saw something similar in python: pad_to sometimes inserts `None` for missing dims. Runtime coerces None->0 on some shards and throws on others, causing mixed failure modes and reorder during fallback.

nina: can you paste a short log + response?

harper: server log snippet: 
```
[2026-09-03T09:12:11Z] incoming batch id=batch-901 size=8 client=node-0.11.0
[2026-09-03T09:12:11Z] dispatch rerank-shard-12 seq=908
[2026-09-03T09:12:12Z] model timeout seq=908
[2026-09-03T09:12:12Z] fallback dispatch rerank-shard-04 seq=908 retry=1
[2026-09-03T09:12:13Z] response sent seq=908 idempotency=missing order_preserved=false
```

harper: response body (trim):
```
{ scores:[0.91,0.83,0.55,0.42,0.21,0.13,0.05,0.01], ids:["r3","r0","r6","r5","r1","r4","r7","r2"] }
```

leo: two things colliding: (1) retry path in JS transport was dropping `x-idempotency-key` so server treated retry as new request and reordered; (2) helper assumed positional stability and zipped scores -> docs by index.

nina: we should always persist an idempotency key per batch and, on response, build a map from returned ids->scores and reattach to originals by id. Fallback to index only if response is truly index-only.

rusty: adding: in the Rust SDK I saw another flaw where the helper flattens `meta` alongside results and zips by index. When ids reorder, meta attaches to wrong doc. We need id->meta reattachment across SDKs.

leo: also a data hygiene bug: padTo in JS returns `undefined` for missing dims if the vector lacks values, which is different from Python's None. This causes cross-lang parity headaches. Let's standardize helper sanitizer: always throw on null/undefined/NaN and list offending id with a short vector preview. Example error: "invalid_vector: id=r17 expected=640 found=632 nulls=8 preview=[0.12,0.14,0.11,...]"

nina: Proposed quick fixes: 
- SDKs: persist per-batch `x-idempotency-key` across retry attempts.
- Helpers: pre-send validation middleware: assert length==model_dim, every entry is finite number, no null/undefined/NaN. Emit clear error with id + preview.
- Post-process: prefer server-returned `ids` array for mapping; build id->score & id->meta maps and reattach. Warn only when falling back to index mapping.

rusty: Tests: add parity test that stubs runtime to return reordered ids on retry, assert SDKs map by id. Add sampleapp CI smoke: 50 burst rerank requests asserting id set and meta alignment.

ci-bot: Created: DX-6120 (sdk: persist idempotency across retries), DX-6121 (helpers: strict vector sanitizer + id-based mapping), DX-6122 (parity tests + sampleapp CI burst).

harper: short-term mitigation: reduce default batch retries to 1 for rerank/embed in Node & Python and add a one-line note in sampleapp quickstart about idempotency header. Longer-term: default to idempotent retries and require server to echo `ids` for batches.

leo: I'll open small Node PR to persist header and change mapping logic. nina: can you handle Python change? rusty: you'll add Rust test.

nina: PRs: node-sdk draft -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/1622, python-sdk draft -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/518, rust parity test -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-parity/pull/77 (all drafts).

harper: thanks team. This explains the customer-reported wrong-snippet bug. :pray:
